I1.quote: Hydrogen (99.999% purity) adsorption isotherms were measured volumetrically using Hiden HTP-1 volumetric sorption analyzer.

I2.quote: AC samples were prepared in a multi-step process from corncob consisting of successive chemical activation by phosphoric acid and potassium hydroxide. ... The boron content in the resulting sample is 1.4 wt %.

I3.quote: Hydrogen gravimetric excess adsorption isotherms were measured at T = 80 K and pressures ranging from 1 to 100 bar.
I3.location: main, p. 4, Experimental, 'Supercritical hydrogen adsorption'; also Fig. 4 (p. 5), axis 'Pressure (bar)', panel label '80K'

I4.quote: The samples specific surface was 3300 m2/g before, and 3100 m2/g after irradiation.
I4.location: main, p. 4, Results and Discussion (BET method stated p. 3, 'Subcritical nitrogen adsorption')

I5.quote: This work investigates the effects of neutron irradiation on nitrogen and hydrogen adsorption in boron-doped activated carbon.

notes: Sorbent is boron-doped (1.4 wt% B) KOH/H3PO4-activated corncob carbon, before and after 1 min neutron irradiation; majority carbon, so a carbon sorbent (doped_carbon). H2 isotherms (excess and 'total amount stored', g H2/kg carbon) at 80 K, 0-100 bar, Fig. 4; 80 K is outside the 76.0-79.0 K window of the 77 K definition. Room-temperature result mentioned qualitatively only, with no value. BET area by N2 at 77 K, P/P0 0.01-0.03. No retraction notice; no statement that the H2 data were published before. Paper also contains modeling (fission-track and Ono-Kondo fits), but uptake is measured.
